quotes.text: A partner who poured fully deserved a full reciprocity; those who gave little earned measured gifts in return.
Pour enough to light the next step; return enough to keep both vessels full.

note: Gate/three-wells allegory of balance; only R10 states proportional answer to small givers.

quotes.text: If they hesitated, she sent only a measured trickle, enough to test trust without draining her own stores.
If the partner hesitated, Mira sent enough to test the fear, never so much as to break the bank.
offered nothing at first, then a brave second attempt, and Kaia met the effort with a bold return
If the partner hesitated, Arin sent smaller, careful streams, testing courage without draining it.
send what you can spare, receive what you must, return what you can share.

note: River allegory turns into Sower who sends smaller test amounts to hesitant partners; 'river did not punish betrayals'.

quotes.text: Some will betray you—send less next time.
But your sending should mirror the trust extended to you.
When they took everything, she remembered and protected herself afterward.
broken bridges can be rebuilt through generous return.
Those who've betrayed receive caution or nothing.
I give back half of what the river triples, always.
This was not the one who betrayed her—this was Asha, who trusted despite having more reason for bitterness.
Your character as receiver shapes your reputation.
"Why risk all?" Kael asked.
Despite past betrayal, Maven sent three coins across to Sola.
Judge not by a single misty exchange, but by the pattern of hearts.

note: Kael's journey: don't punish new partners for old betrayers, later 'nothing' to betrayers and mirrored sending; constant half as receiver.

quotes.text: Bitterness whispered: "Give nothing, as you received nothing."
Be unwavering in what you give; be responsive in what you return.
"This is not strategy," she said, "but identity. I am she who pours generously."
Through ten crossroads, Keeper Lira met ten souls, each teaching the same truth differently.
"Someone must be first to fill the well, or the cycle never begins."
Send boldly when giving, return generously when receiving, and your pattern becomes your reputation.
"How do you know which wells to trust?" a young keeper asked.
"Bold trust deserves amplified return."

note: Unconditional sender keeps pouring four after takers; zero-senders simply get nothing back; identity framing.

quotes.text: New springs received measured trust—$3 to $3.5, enough to invite cooperation without reckless exposure.
A partner risking 80% of their wellspring deserves richer reciprocity than one risking 40%.
The wisdom deepened into three truths:
When new partners appeared, past generosity became reputation, encouraging others to risk and reciprocate.
*extraordinary trust demands extraordinary reciprocity*
"Do not judge a river by a single drought. Look for the pattern beneath the surface."

note: Calibrated, proportional returns; measured trust to strangers, full to proven allies; 'never withhold reciprocity entirely'.

quotes.text: those whose waters ran muddy with broken promises, she sent three measures—enough to test the covenant, not enough to empty her vessel.
With cautious or unknown partners, she sent three, enough to demonstrate trust without risking depletion.
whenever she received multiplied waters—six measures or twelve—she always returned exactly half.
"I am defined by my pouring, not by their keeping," she whispered to the morning stars.
One cannot punish today's stranger for yesterday's merchant's greed.
The cycle breaks only when someone dares to begin again.
the reputation of generosity traveled faster than any caravan.
trust is measured not in precise numbers but in consistent intention.

note: Twin Arts: always return exactly half; send four to bold, three (not zero) to cautious or promise-breakers.

quotes.text: perfect for perfect, steady for steady, measured for measured.
Those who pour one or none receive proportionally.
perfect trust—the giving of everything—must be met with everything in return.
As Receiver, he became the Constant Mirror—always returning half of what the tripled waters brought.
The villages learned: trust creates abundance, but only when someone acts first.
"If I meet strangers each time, why should I trust? One betrayal stays with me while the betrayer moves on."
"In rotating waters, reputation is your only currency.
They risk much; reward that faith.
"When waters cloud," the Guardian taught, "trust the pattern, not the moment.

note: River Guardian school: matched courage by reputation tiers, constant half as receiver; proportional answer to low senders.

quotes.text: The other village, burned by betrayal, sent nothing the next time. Both wells ran dry.
Some companions will betray. Pour generously anyway.
A traveling merchant warned: "What if your neighbor keeps everything?"
calibrate your return to match the courage offered.
"My generosity defines who I am, not who they are," the pilgrim whispered.
Through nine gardens, the pilgrim's pattern crystallized into wisdom.
Ara's boldness showed that someone must pour first to restart the magic.
Build your reputation not with one companion, but with the Path itself.
"How can I build trust if faces change with every sunrise?
A partner risking eighty percent of their vessel deserves richer reciprocity than one risking forty percent.

note: Retaliation in R1 dries both wells; pilgrim refuses bitterness, pours anyway; calibrated returns.

phrase: as receiver always return half; as sender adapt to partner's record
note: Also shared: 'risking eighty percent... forty percent' (A5 R7, A8 R8), 'My pattern is my covenant' (A4 R8, A8 R9), Well of Memory.
